title: EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
why: Financial entities and critical ICT systems under DORA must classify and report major ICT-related incidents within strict statutory windows, prove operational continuity and recovery under disruption, and maintain an enforceable register and exit strategy for third-party ICT providers.

addRequirements.title: Major ICT incidents are classified and logged on a reporting clock
addRequirements.statement: When an operational outage, data-integrity failure or security anomaly occurs, the application shall record a structured ICT incident with severity criteria, affected services, client-impact count and detection timestamp to support initial, intermediate and final DORA regulatory reports.
addRequirements.definition: Incident triage uses deterministic thresholds rather than ad-hoc judgement so statutory notification clocks start automatically on detection.
addRequirements.failurePath: If impact telemetry is incomplete at detection time, the incident defaults to escalated review and records the detection timestamp immediately rather than delaying classification.
acceptance: Given a fault crossing configured availability or data-integrity thresholds, when detected, then a structured incident record is persisted with detection time, classification and escalation deadline.
Given a classified major incident, when an incident report export is generated, then it includes initial, intermediate and root-cause timeline fields without mutating earlier entries.

addRequirements.title: Critical functions degrade predictably and verify backup integrity
addRequirements.statement: When a primary dependency or storage node fails, the application shall enforce bounded timeouts, preserve transactional integrity without silent data loss, and verify backup integrity hashes before restore.
addRequirements.definition: Recovery time and recovery point objectives are backed by deterministic failure handling and verified restore artifacts.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a backup fails integrity verification or a failover target is unhealthy, the application aborts automated promotion and alerts the on-call operator.
acceptance: Given a simulated dependency outage, when requests hit a critical workflow, then the application fails closed with no partial state corruption and emits a recovery metric.
Given a backup artifact with a tampered checksum, when restore verification runs, then the restore is rejected.

addRequirements.title: Third-party ICT dependencies carry a register of information and exit path
addRequirements.statement: The application shall maintain a machine-readable register of every third-party ICT provider naming criticality, data location, contractual audit rights and fallback or exit adapter, and refuse unregistered outbound ICT integrations.
addRequirements.definition: Concentration risk and exit readiness stay coupled to actual runtime integrations rather than a stale spreadsheet.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a critical workflow enables an external ICT provider missing from the register or lacking a declared exit plan, startup validation or CI rejects the configuration.
acceptance: Given an external provider not listed in the ICT register, when configuration is validated, then validation fails naming the unregistered provider.
Given a registered critical provider, when its entry is inspected, then service scope, region, criticality tier and exit mechanism are all populated.

addGates.statement: ICT incident classification, backup-integrity verification and the third-party ICT provider register are proven by automated tests.
